mods.name: Salts Mills
mods.description: An aspirational dream for better times with questionable noises

releases.notes:
There is probably something in testing mods in both actual client and server situations rather than just via Gradle. Turns out Fabric's dedicated server classloading is most unlike client or dev time. The results of this can be found in #1.

Salts Mill legitimately now works on a server, regardless of whether any of the cassettes it can load does too. Refmap warnings are now all gone too after a Loom update which allowed each jar to have its own refmap name.

### Installation
As per [v0.1](https://github.com/Chocohead/Modjam/releases/tag/v0.1). Big cassette is still unchanged so isn't rehosted here.

releases.notes:
Sometimes it doesn't matter how well you design your features if you then go and don't use them. As such as many listeners as you'd like can be run on a single side, but if you don't tell it to none of them will!

The example cassette now actually works on a server rather than just claiming to. Also ensures future errors are actually properly handled without hanging the game thread (even if most likely it did manage to print the problem in the log).

### Installation
As per [v0.1](https://github.com/Chocohead/Modjam/releases/tag/v0.1). Big cassette is still unchanged so isn't rehosted here.

releases.notes:
From what happened in v0.2, `ProtoModMetadata` is gone and `ModMetadata` is now the only form again. Type safety is just as poor as before but at least there's less duplication about now. Cassettes can now specify the type of mod they have a dependency on to allow depending on more than just Salts Mill ones. Cassette resource loading can be debugged with `chocohead.sm.slot.debug=true` as a system property (ie run with `-Dchocohead.sm.slot.debug=true` as a VM argument).

The example cassette now properly handles both the lack and presence of Fabric's Item Group API. No tabs will be lost on the pages now, and it'll always pick Building Blocks rather than occasionally going a page too early.

### Installation
As per [v0.1](https://github.com/Chocohead/Modjam/releases/tag/v0.1). Big cassette is unchanged so isn't rehosted here.

releases.notes:
Apparently some mods are not the biggest of fans being classloaded completely out of order. The moral of the story is for people to test their mods in a variety of scenarios to improve hardiness. In the meantime my beautiful type safety is in tatters.

Only change is to Salts Mill itself to shift classloading listeners to just before they are first called rather than game start. Leaves a strange sameness between `ProtoModMetadata` and `ModMetadata`, but that's quick fixes for you.

### Installation
As per [v0.1](https://github.com/Chocohead/Modjam/releases/tag/v0.1). Also has the cassettes to save rehosting the same files for no reason.
